image_description: Two male mallard ducks (drakes) swimming in brown water. The duck in the foreground is fully visible, displaying an iridescent green head, white neck ring, grey body, and black tail with curled feathers. A second drake is partially visible behind it, showing a similar green head and yellow bill. Both are floating on the water surface.

The eyes of the foreground duck are clearly visible as small, dark spots on the side of the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The foreground duck exhibits a classic streamlined, buoyant shape sitting low in the water. Plumage appears dense and smooth.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows the specific mallard pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, grey flanks, and brownish chest.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ducks are swimming; legs and feet are submerged and completely occluded by the water and body angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rear of the foreground duck clearly displays the characteristic upward-curling black tail feathers typical of male mallards.
